oewn-07566518-n.learner: the way a person feels, either as a habit or for a short time
examples: She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper.
Your tempers are by no means unlike.
She flew into a temper when she heard the news.
His temper cooled as fast as it had flared.

oewn-04649615-n.learner: a tendency to show anger that a person does not control
examples: He has a temper, and everyone at work knows to keep out of his way.

connotation.why: names a fault of character rather than a neutral trait

oewn-06701019-n.learner: approval given to someone for something
examples: your uncle would never have yielded, if we had not given him credit for another interest in the affair
She never got the credit she deserved for the idea.

oewn-00037921-n.learner: used in the phrase 'to your credit' to show that something you have done deserves praise
examples: To her credit, she admitted the mistake at once.
He has three novels to his credit.

oewn-13395454-n.learner: an arrangement that lets you take goods or services now and pay for them later
examples: The shop let them buy the coal on credit and settle at the end of the month.

oewn-05953807-n.learner: what you believe, or picture in your mind, that the future will be like
examples: But as Elizabeth could not receive comfort from any such expectation she made no answer.
their astonishment was beyond their expectation

oewn-14509706-n.learner: looking forward to something you are sure will happen
examples: in the expectation of his arrival, Elizabeth could easily perceive that her spirits were affected by it
It was a comfort to Elizabeth to consider that Jane could not have been wearied by long expectations.

oewn-07526162-n.learner: the feeling that something is just about to happen
examples: She sat still in the dark hall, full of expectation that the door would open at any moment.

oewn-02012411-v.learner: to go away, or to leave a place
examples: Elizabeth heard him the next moment open the front door and quit the house.
Elizabeth did not quit her room for a moment, nor were the other ladies often absent

oewn-02686624-v.learner: to put an end to a state or an activity
examples: He quit smoking last year.
I wish they would quit arguing about it.

oewn-02387509-v.learner: to give up a position, or to retire from it
examples: She quit her job at the bank in the spring.

oewn-05175788-n.learner: the quality of mattering and being worth taking notice of
examples: I have sent for you on an affair of importance.
One day's delay, she observed, would be of small importance

oewn-14458147-n.learner: a high, noticeable position among other people
examples: Our importance, our respectability in the world, must be affected by the wild volatility, the assurance and disdain of all restraint
He was a man of some importance in the town.

oewn-00761314-v.learner: to ask someone humbly and earnestly to do something
examples: I beg you will not put it into Lizzy's head to be vexed by his ill-treatment
I beg you to think again before you answer him.

oewn-00784104-v.learner: to ask for something in an urgent way, or to keep asking for it
examples: Jane has written to beg my uncle's immediate assistance, and we shall be off, I hope, in half an hour
Kitty begged very hard for a few balls there every winter.

oewn-02275660-v.learner: to ask people to give you something without paying for it
examples: He was begging for coins outside the station.

connotation.why: casts the asker as living on other people's charity

oewn-00156409-v.learner: to become bigger, or to become greater in amount
examples: The advice was followed readily, for the feverish symptoms increased, and her head ached acutely.
the perturbation of Elizabeth's feelings was every moment increasing

oewn-00153083-v.learner: to make something bigger, or to make there be more of it
examples: It was not in her nature, however, to increase her vexations by dwelling on them.
Her astonishment, as she reflected on what had passed, was increased by every review of it.

oewn-06753097-n.learner: a good reason for something to exist or to happen
examples: she found little other cause for satisfaction in the loss of the regiment
was dismissed from her charge on some cause of disapprobation, though he did not say what

oewn-07341157-n.learner: the events that make something else come about
examples: it is impossible for us to conjecture the causes or circumstances which may have alienated them

oewn-00007347-n.learner: anything or anyone that produces an effect, or that is responsible for what happens
examples: he was the cause--his pride and caprice were the cause--of all that Jane had suffered

oewn-00816521-a.learner: at or near the start of a stretch of time or a run of events, or before the usual or expected time
examples: Mr. Bennet was among the earliest of those who waited on Mr. Bingley.
Mrs. Bennet, through the assistance of servants, contrived to have the earliest tidings of it
a favourite with her mother, whose affection had brought her into public at an early age

oewn-00820993-a.learner: being or happening at an early point in how something develops
examples: The illness can be treated if it is caught in its early stages.
Is her husband, who is the son of his late father's steward, to be his brother?
A younger son, you know, must be inured to self-denial and dependence.
